name: The Great Glasshouse

text: Iron and glass, two hundred feet of it, warm as a summer nobody ordered.
GIVEN TO THE CITY. NOT OWNED BY IT.
There is a second, smaller line under that giving the donor. It is the Foundation.
Reed beds under glass, grown from wetland stock, with a card explaining
that they are here because the wetlands are drying and somebody
wanted a copy kept somewhere the weather could not reach.
Coastal grasses in a long tray of imported sand.
Nine species. Two of them no longer grow anywhere on the actual coast.
The card does not make a fuss about this and somehow that is worse.
A young tree with a rail round it and a plaque at the foot.
It is a cutting from the great bell tree at Briarbell, taken forty years ago.
It is doing well. It is a fifth the size.
A bed of flowering scrub that only opens after a hot night,
and a bench in front of it that is the most-booked bench in the city.
There is a waiting list. For a bench.
The shallow pool. Ankle-deep, warm, and full of small things
that are not afraid of you.
A card asks you to walk through it slowly. Everyone does.
A release register. Every Kin bred by the conservation programme,
where it went, and the date. Four thousand lines this year.
Anybody may add a sighting. The margin is full of other people's handwriting.
A bed left deliberately unplanted, roped off, with a card on a post.
THIS IS WHAT THIS ROOM LOOKS LIKE WITHOUT US.
It is a small square of dry grey soil and it is very effective.
A trunk with a hundred names cut into it, some of them a century old.
The gardeners stopped fighting it around 1030 and started dating them instead.
The most recent is from this morning and is spelled wrong.
A bed of the flowers that grow along the central road, kept for people
who have moved to the capital and cannot go home often.
It is the only bed in the glasshouse with a bin beside it for handkerchiefs.

_plan: The Grand Park's glasshouse, and the single most sympathetic thing the Foundation has built. Everything in it is a copy kept somewhere the weather cannot reach, which is Cassian's whole argument stated gently by a gardener. The unplanted roped-off square saying THIS IS WHAT THIS ROOM LOOKS LIKE WITHOUT US is the closest the game comes to letting him make his case before he makes it.
